dedupe_keys.name: sustain system for urban stormwater treatment and analysis integration

description: SUSTAIN is an EPA decision support system for developing, evaluating and selecting optimal combinations of stormwater best management practices, including green infrastructure, at various watershed scales based on cost and effectiveness. It covers hydrologic and water quality modelling in watersheds and urban streams with seven modules on a common ArcGIS platform, including a framework manager, a BMP siting tool that screens locations by drainage area, soil group, groundwater depth and buffers, land simulation with algorithms adapted from SWMM 5 and HSPF, BMP simulation and optimisation; point BMPs include bioretention, cisterns, rain barrels, infiltration basins and wetlands, linear BMPs include swales and filter strips, and area BMPs include porous pavement and green roofs. It was developed by the US EPA, which is no longer developing or supporting it and has no plans for updates. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): EPA web policy: EPA-produced content is in the public domain unless otherwise specified (software licence not stated separately). Caveats: the GIS build needs ESRI ArcGIS 9.3 with Spatial Analyst and Excel, and the software is unsupported. It remains useful for optimising placement and sizing of green-blue stormwater infrastructure for water quality and climate adaptation planning; a related record is the EPA National Stormwater Calculator.
